wholePhysicalScope: Named Danya Hill enclosure and measured gallery footprints from the Shandong and Penglai gazetteers. The verified 1925 plate sets the approach silhouette.
lodDetails: All four levels retain the twin roof profiles, galleries and flanking approach. Nearer levels add screen frames, rails, brackets and roof seams.
limitations: The reconstruction depicts the central Penglai Pavilion, its stone terrace and the paired flanking rooms, circa December 1925. Nearby temples and harbor walls are outside this model.

The main pavilion uses the 14.80 m by 9.65 m lower gallery dimensions given by the county gazetteer; the Shandong heritage survey gives a depth of 9.85 m. Bay spacing, side rooms, stairs, bracket detailing and timber tint are estimated.
The larger mapped enclosure sets the alignment. The hall position within it is approximate. Elevations were sampled from a 30 m terrain source and the original landform is preserved.
